overview: The Sagarmala Programme is a flagship initiative of the Government of India aimed at promoting port-led development through the harnessing of India's 7,500 km long coastline, 14,500 km of potentially navigable waterways and strategic location on key international maritime trade routes. It seeks to reduce logistics costs for both domestic and EXIM cargo, enhance port infrastructure, and promote industrialization and coastal community development. The programme integrates the development of ports, industrial clusters, hinterland connectivity, and coastal shipping to drive economic growth and job creation.
objectives: Reduce logistics cost for EXIM and domestic cargo through optimized infrastructure investment
Modernize and mechanize ports to achieve global standards of efficiency
Develop new major ports and enhance capacity of existing ports
Enhance evacuation infrastructure to and from ports via rail, road, inland waterways and pipelines
Promote port-led industrialization and development of coastal economic zones
Develop inland waterways and coastal shipping as sustainable and cost-effective transport modes
Skill development and livelihood enhancement for coastal communities
Enhance sustainability and environmental protection in port and coastal areas
eligibility: Eligibility varies by component and project under Sagarmala. Generally, proposals are invited from state governments, maritime boards, port trusts, central public sector enterprises, and private sector entities through competitive bidding or public-private partnership (PPP) modes. Projects must align with the National Perspective Plan (NPP) under Sagarmala and contribute to port-led development.
benefits: Benefits include reduced logistics costs, improved port efficiency and capacity, enhanced hinterland connectivity, promotion of coastal shipping and inland waterways, development of industrial clusters and manufacturing zones, job creation in port and coastal areas, skill development for local communities, and increased exports and economic growth through port-led development.
financial_support: Financial support under Sagarmala is provided through various mechanisms including budgetary allocations from the Government of India, extra-budgetary resources, private investment via PPP, institutional financing from banks and financial institutions, and viability gap funding (VGF) where applicable. The programme leverages convergence with other central and state schemes, and financial support is extended based on project appraisal and approval under the institutional framework of Sagarmala.
application_process: 1. Identification of project ideas aligned with Sagarmala objectives and National Perspective Plan (NPP). 2. Preparation of Detailed Project Report (DPR) by the project proponent. 3. Submission of proposal to the concerned nodal agency (e.g., Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, State Government, or Port Trust). 4. Appraisal of the project by the Sagarmala Coordination and Steering Committee (SCSC) or relevant technical committee. 5. Approval by the Empowered Committee under Sagarmala. 6. Implementation of the project through EPC contracts or PPP mode. 7. Monitoring and evaluation by the Sagarmala Secretariat and concerned ministries.
required_documents: Board resolution or authorization from the sponsoring entity
Incorporation documents of the project SPV (if applicable)
deadlines: Rolling basis — proposals are accepted throughout the year based on budget availability and project readiness.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
caveats: Projects must conform to the National Perspective Plan (NPP) under Sagarmala
Environmental and Coastal Regulation Zone (CRZ) clearances are mandatory where applicable
Land acquisition and rehabilitation & resettlement (R&R) must comply with central and state laws
Private sector participation requires adherence to PPP guidelines and transparent bidding processes
Financial support is subject to availability of funds and project appraisal outcomes
